chapter: Philadelphia, Detroit and back to Atlantic City
title: Crazy Blues, phonographs and wind-up records
summary: He says Perry Bradford deserved the credit for Crazy Blues and that few Black households had wind-up phonographs.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Bessie, Mamie, Ma Rainey: the classic blues queens

blocks.x: Right. Well, that leads me to my next question, which is, in 1920, Mamie Smith recorded, you know, the "Crazy Blues", and all of a sudden black singers started recording which they hadn't before. Do you remember, I mean, "Crazy Blues", they say, was a very big hit. Do you remember that being a big hit? Do you remember hearing these records?
Yes, it was a very big hit. But a lot of people don't give the right credit, to the right people. The man that's due credit is Perry Bradford.

Oh, sure. No, no, I'm not talking about that. I know that. But, I wanted to know if you, being in Atlantic City around that time, remember suddenly there being records, and did you for instance, listen to records? Did you have a phonograph or did you know someone who had one. That was a whole new thing for black people, wasn't it?
Well, we didn't listen too much to records, because most blacks, there wasn't a lot of them had phonographs, you know what I mean?
And at that time they were the old fashioned phonographs that you'd wind up, you know?
No electric phonographs or record players. It was all wind up. And then, some people had them. And the portable ones hadn't taken hold yet, you know?

So it was only when maybe they'd buy one and run it in a cabaret, like this was a new innovation or something like that, but otherwise it wasn't known. But we heard about the 'Crazy Blues' and Mamie Smith for the simple reason why. So many people was always coming back from New York to Atlantic City all the time, cause now Atlantic City was the summer Mecca, while New York was the winter Mecca, you know what I mean? Of the people in the life.
Because if you wasn't in the life, you didn't go to cabarets in those days.
